description: Intent i039 (alloc-multiply-overflow, snapshot s10) complete. FINDING: drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c:218-240 (quote 'num_pages = (param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) >> PAGE_SHIFT;', confidence medium) — ioctl FSL_HV_IOCTL_MEMCPY copies a fully userspace-controlled u64 param.count via copy_from_user (line 165); the check at 218-220 guards only 64-bit wraparound, while the assignment at 221 truncates the 64-bit sum into 'unsigned int num_pages' with no clamp; kmalloc(num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) + sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) - 1) at lines 239-240 is a plain 32-bit multiply-add with no overflow-checked sizing, so num_pages ~2^29 wraps the product to ~0 and the fill loop 'for (i = 1; i < num_pages; i++)' at line 274 writes 32-byte sg_list[i] entries far past the undersized buffer — the seed's truncated-product->undersized-alloc->element-indexed-write chain from a local ioctl attacker. Counterevidence checked: the sibling allocation at line 229 uses overflow-checked kzalloc_objs/size_mul, and the seed usbip path is PATCHED in s10 (usbip_common.c:685 clamps np to [0, USBIP_MAX_ISO_PACKETS], zeroes urb->number_of_packets, and uses kcalloc at 699). Candidates classified: ldm.c:1247 safe (num clamped [1,4] and only caller's perbuf=512/size bound), sctp sm_make_chunk.c:3653 safe (truncated stream_len is used consistently for alloc and copies), be_cmds.c:2929 safe (feeds bounds check, not allocator), pvrdma_mr.c:218, vfio_ccw_cp.c:514, gve_adminq.c:1160 safe; fbcmap.c:95 left unresolved (s10 entry-path clamp not re-verified). Bounded negative evidence: two regex families (narrow-typed size=count*sizeof assignments, allocator calls with inline multiplies) run tree-wide over drivers/fs/net/block/sound/crypto; 'count << shift' and memcpy-length families not run. Limitations: no runtime reproducer; exploitation needs ~2^27+ pinnable pages and root-owned /dev/fsl-hv on Freescale powerpc; multiple sweep hits (ipu6/ipu7-dma, fuse file.c, xfs_inode_fork, ethtool bitset, rds message.c, state_dump, dimmtemp, atomisp) located but not deep-read. Artifact: agent-state/findings/i039.json.
